sections.h2: Where is Belmont County, Ohio, and who lives there?
sections.html:
Belmont County fills a stretch of Ohio's eastern border, where the Ohio River separates it from West Virginia. Wikipedia lists 541.27 square miles of area, most of it low rolling hills cut by creeks such as Captina and McMahon. St. Clairsville is the county seat, and Martins Ferry is the largest city.

The county was created on September 7, 1801, and has kept its present boundaries since 1813. Coal, the National Road and the river trade shaped it early. Bellaire counted 15 glass factories by 1881 and was called the Glass City. Today the county is part of the Wheeling metropolitan area.

The 2020 census counted 66,497 people. The 2025 estimate is 64,434, which is 3.1 percent lower. Almost 25 percent of residents are 65 or older, which bears on the homestead credit discussed below. Public high schools sit in Bellaire, Bridgeport, Martins Ferry, Saint Clairsville and Shadyside, and Buckeye Local and Union Local have high schools of their own.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Belmont County homes?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau's QuickFacts page for Belmont County shows a modest, owner-heavy market. Survey years are 2020 to 2024 except where a bullet says otherwise.

  • Typical owner-occupied home value: $154,900.
  • Owner-occupied housing unit rate: 73.6 percent, across 27,195 households.
  • Median gross rent: $793 a month.
  • Median household income: $57,017, with 15.1 percent of residents in poverty.
  • Mean commute: 25.1 minutes.
  • Permits issued during 2025: 2.

The county auditor's own site lists 76,512 parcels. Ask the treasurer for the balance on a given parcel number.

sections.h2: Which Belmont County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
A seller can finish every step inside the courthouse at 101 West Main Street, St. Clairsville. One office sets the value, one sends the bill, and one files the deed.

  • Auditor. Sets values, takes board of revision complaints and endorses deeds. The main line is 740-699-2130, real estate is 740-699-2132, and the deed transfer desk is 740-699-2136. Walk-in service runs weekdays, 8:30 to 4:30.
  • Treasurer. Mails the bills and takes payment. Phone 740-699-2145 on weekdays, 8:30 to 4:30.
  • Recorder. Files deeds and mortgages and, in the recorder's words, looks after more than 220 years of county land records. The office does not run title searches.

The treasurer can give the rate of taxation for your district, which varies with the school and village levies.

sections.h2: When are Belmont County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Real estate tax comes in two installments, mailed in January and June. By the treasurer's FAQ, the due dates usually fall in the third week of February and of July, unless the bill says otherwise.

Belmont County tax calendar for 2025 taxes payable in 2026
ItemDate or rule
First-half bills mailedThird week of January 2026
First half dueFriday, February 20, 2026
Second-half bills mailedWeek of July 1, 2026
Second half dueFriday, July 24, 2026
Late penalty5 percent inside ten days, 10 percent after
Valuation complaint windowJanuary 1 to March 31

Source: Belmont County Treasurer, treasurer FAQ and auditor timeline.

A postmark counts as timely, and the treasurer suggests carrying the envelope into the post office so it gets stamped. A secure drop box sits on the left side of the courthouse front stairs and is open only during the January and February and June and July collection periods. Cash does not go in the box.

Ohio bills taxes one year behind. Ohio taxes run in arrears, so a bill arriving in 2026 covers tax year 2025.

sections.h2: What happens when a Belmont County tax payment is late?
sections.html:
The county adds a penalty first and interest later. Under Ohio Revised Code 323.121, a ten percent penalty attaches to an unpaid half, and interest on older delinquent tax runs at the rate set under section 5703.47.

The treasurer's FAQ is blunt on two points. A missing bill is no excuse, since the owner is responsible under section 323.13. A request to remit the penalty can still be filed when something outside the owner's control got in the way, such as hospitalization, a prolonged illness or the death of an immediate family member.

Owners who are behind should call 740-699-2145 and ask about payment options. The statute recognizes delinquent tax contracts, and while one stays in effect no ten percent penalty is added to the covered first-half taxes after the second-half collection period.

If back taxes go unpaid long enough, the parcel can reach tax foreclosure. The auditor's office has run forfeited land sales for parcels that failed to sell at foreclosure. The opening bid equals current taxes plus court costs, and the winning bidder pays the deed, conveyance and recording fees. Selling the house before that point keeps the proceeds with the owner.

sections.h2: How do you challenge a Belmont County valuation?
sections.html:
A valuation complaint is filed at the auditor's office. Ohio Revised Code 5715.19 gives owners until the later of two dates: the last day of March following the tax year, or the day first-half collection closes. The treasurer's FAQ tells owners March 31.

The hearing notice must reach the owner at least ten days beforehand. A mailed complaint is judged by its United States postmark, and a private meter mark does not count. Taxing bodies such as a school board can file their own complaints or counter-complaints, so the district may appear at the hearing.

Belmont County's latest reappraisal ran on this path:

  • January 2022: the Ohio Department of Taxation ordered the reappraisal for tax year 2024.
  • April 2022: data mailers went to every property with a dwelling.
  • Summer and fall 2024: informal reviews with owners.
  • October 2024: final values went to the state.
  • January 2025: bills with the new values were mailed, and the complaint window ran January 1 to March 31, 2025.

Ohio generally limits an owner to one complaint per interim period, with listed exceptions such as an improvement added to the property or a 15 percent swing in occupancy. Ask the auditor which year Belmont County sits in before filing.

sections.h2: Which tax breaks can a Belmont County owner claim?
sections.html:
The homestead exemption is the main one. The Ohio Department of Taxation publishes the tax year 2026 table: $29,700 of market value shielded for low-income seniors and disabled owners, $59,400 for disabled veterans, and a $41,000 income limit on the first group.

Send the application to the auditor before the year ends, because the credit is tied to the calendar year. A denied application can go to the board of revision on form DTE 106B, filed within 60 days of the notice. The treasurer's site also carries the homestead application for seniors, disabled residents and surviving spouses.

The credit does not pass with the deed, so the buyer qualifies on his or her own. That is why the deed paperwork asks about it, as the next section explains.

sections.h2: How is tax handled when a Belmont County house sells?
sections.html:
The auditor's endorsement is the first step on a deed. Section 319.202 has the buyer or a representative file a statement of value. That filing must say the seller was asked about any homestead or owner-occupancy tax cut on the house. If the seller answered yes, a sworn estimate of the cut is attached.

The auditor's value-statement fee comes from section 319.54(G)(3): a flat dollar or ten cents per hundred, whichever is higher. The same section lists exempt transfers, among them gifts within a family. Section 322.02 also lets a county levy a deed transfer tax capped at 30 cents per $100. Ask the deed transfer desk at 740-699-2136 for Belmont County's current conveyance rate.

A seller who still gets a bill after closing is told to review the closing papers and then contact the title company, banker or agent. Unpaid tax that the closing statement never addressed can stay with the owner. Pay off or prorate the bill at the table.

faqs.q: Does Belmont County collect the second half in July?
faqs.a: Yes. Expect the second half around the third week of July. The 2025 tax year bills fell due on Friday, February 20, 2026 (first half) and Friday, July 24, 2026 (second half). Mailing happens in January and in June or early July, and the printed date on your bill controls.

faqs.q: Who values a house in Belmont County?
faqs.a: The county auditor values every parcel, and the auditor's office lists 76,512 of them. The treasurer only bills and collects. Complaints about value are filed with the auditor, whose office serves as the board's secretary.

faqs.q: How steep is the Belmont County late penalty?
faqs.a: A payment inside the ten-day grace window draws 5 percent. Later than that, the treasurer's notice puts it at 10 percent of what is still owed for the current year. The statute also adds interest on older delinquent tax. A penalty remission request is possible for circumstances beyond your control.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Belmont County house with back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Phone 740-699-2145 for the payoff number, and the title company can pay it off at closing. A sale ahead of any tax foreclosure keeps the decision with you, where a forfeited land sale ends it.

faqs.q: Can the buyer keep my homestead reduction?
faqs.a: No. The credit belongs to the qualifying owner who lives in the home. The deed paperwork asks the seller about any reduction. A buyer who qualifies must apply separately. Applications go to the auditor, with a December 31 cutoff.
